subject: Physics
description: Radio, microwave, IR, visible, UV, X-ray, gamma

questions.stem: The EM wave with the longest wavelength among the following is:
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic spectrum (longest-wavelength / lowest-frequency first): Radio → Microwave → Infrared → Visible → Ultraviolet → X-ray → Gamma ray. Radio waves range from ~1 mm up to many kilometres. Mnemonic — 'Roman Men Invented Very Unusual Xtravagant Gadgets'.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The speed of light (and of all EM waves) in vacuum is approximately:
questions.explanation: c = 2.998 × 10⁸ m/s in vacuum ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s. Inside a medium, light slows by a factor equal to the refractive index n (~1.5 for glass, ~1.33 for water). c is a fundamental constant of nature — defined exactly since the 1983 re-definition of the metre. Sound travels ~10⁶ times slower than light.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The part of the EM spectrum used to heat food in a microwave oven is:
questions.explanation: Microwave ovens use microwaves at ~2.45 GHz, which are strongly absorbed by water molecules. The water molecules rotate rapidly, generating heat through friction. Infrared is used by remote controls, night-vision cameras, thermal imaging. Radio — communication. X-ray — medical imaging (shorter wavelength, higher energy, ionising).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The EM waves most commonly used for broadcasting radio and television signals are:
questions.explanation: AM radio — ~1 MHz; FM radio — ~100 MHz; TV — higher frequency radio; mobile 4G / 5G — GHz range (entering the microwave regime). All of these are radio waves in the broad sense. Radio waves have long wavelengths and low photon energy, so they are non-ionising and generally safe. Gamma rays and X-rays are ionising and cause cell damage; visible light is what we see.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: X-rays, used in medical imaging, were discovered in 1895 by:
questions.explanation: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen (Germany) discovered X-rays in 1895; he won the first Nobel Prize in Physics, 1901. He called them 'X' rays to denote the unknown nature at the time. Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896 (shared 1903 Physics Nobel with the Curies). Marie Curie discovered polonium and radium (two Nobels — 1903 Physics, 1911 Chemistry). Einstein's 1905 breakthroughs — photoelectric effect (Nobel 1921), special relativity, Brownian motion, E=mc².
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: Visible light forms only a small window of the EM spectrum, with wavelengths ranging approximately from:
questions.explanation: Visible light — ~400-700 nanometres. Shorter — ultraviolet (causes sunburn and Vitamin-D synthesis). Longer — infrared (felt as heat, beyond red). VIBGYOR gives the colours from shortest to longest visible wavelength (Violet ~400, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red ~700). Newton split sunlight through a prism into this spectrum.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: Infrared radiation is detected by our skin as:
questions.explanation: Infrared — 'below red' (longer than red visible light) — carries less energy per photon than visible light but is emitted copiously by warm objects. Our skin receptors perceive IR as heat. Applications — night-vision, remote controls, thermal imaging cameras, laser keyboards. Sunlight has about 50 % of its energy in IR. Greenhouse gases trap Earth's outgoing IR.
